deposits.notes: Found through the paper's p. 2 project page, https://ppyyqq.github.io/narrativeloom (HTTP 200; redirected to the trailing-slash URL), whose System link points to this repository. Repository web page and https://api.github.com/repos/PPYYQQ/narrativeloom-system/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 both returned HTTP 200. The API returned a complete, non-truncated tree with 64 file blobs; directories are excluded from n_files, and files lists 50 entries, prioritizing non-cache files. The inventory consists of application source, ten-persona prompts, frontend build assets, configuration, a dependency lockfile, and compiled Python caches. README.md, config/english_agent.py, service/story_service.py, domain/write_req.py, and .gitignore were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/PPYYQQ/narrativeloom-system/main/ and read in memory; each returned HTTP 200. The README describes an Improvised Writing Platform and deployment. The prompt file contains genre personas and templates, and the request/service files define inputs and generation logic, not observed participant records. No participant dataset, condition assignment/order table, survey results, TTCW ratings, analysis dataset, or participant story corpus was found. Template fields such as history_story and current_beats are not data columns from study observations. The three has_* fields refer to study data, not model prompts or input schemas. S2 coverage denotes the system used in the main study, not availability of its data. No repository license file or license statement was found; the project website's CC BY-SA 4.0 license is not assumed to license the repository.

notes:
Read the entire saved markdown, all 841 lines, and checked the 19-page arXiv:2603.07155v1 PDF with PyMuPDF. The document ends with references on p. 19 and contains no appendix. No formal data-availability statement, offer of data on request, preregistration, or supplementary-data notice was found, including in the acknowledgments on p. 17. Quoted statements preserve PDF extraction exactly, including line wraps and line-end hyphenation; in-paper materials and third-party software citations are distinguished in their locators.

The screening form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty strings. The form has no final key and therefore no final.open_items; no missing-statistics list was invented. S1 is the formative interview study. S2 is the 50-person within-subjects comparison of NarrativeLoom and Chatbot; random assignment to presentation order is not established in the paper/form.

The publicly accessible system code and prompts do not permit recomputation of participant means, SDs or SEs by condition, participant-level TTCW aggregates, analyzed counts, or between-participant text diversity. No participant data file was available for reading, so rows_checked and columns_checked are null. Aggregate statistics printed in the paper and its plots were not treated as a participant-data deposit.

Publisher checks: https://doi.org/10.1145/3772318.3790416 and https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3772318.3790416 both returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' bot-check page. No attempt was made to pass it. Whether ACM hosts additional supplementary files remains unverified; this is not evidence that data require an account.

Additional public-source checks: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07155 returned HTTP 200 and lists only v1, submitted 7 March 2026. Its observed TeX Source link, https://arxiv.org/src/2603.07155, returned HTTP 200; the 5,137,102-byte archive was inspected entirely in memory. Its 24 files comprise the manuscript/configuration TeX files, bibliography and style files, 16 figure files, and 00README.json. That JSON was parsed and contains only source/build metadata (sources, spec_version, texlive_version, process), not participant observations. No participant data or analysis scripts were in the archive. A commented earlier project URL in main.tex, https://ppyyqq.github.io/improviser/, returned HTTP 200 and displayed the same NarrativeLoom page and System repository link. The public project page describes its own website license as CC BY-SA 4.0; arXiv links to CC BY 4.0 for the preprint.

Search follow-up: https://underline.io/lecture/119611-improviser-multi-persona-co-creation-system-enhances-story-creativity returned HTTP 200. This is a potentially related earlier conference presentation with overlapping authors, not a verified participant-data deposit. Its visible downloads are a paper and a transcript. The earlier title was also searched in all four deposit indexes. No claim of shared participants between that presentation and c478 was inferred.

Other repository links printed in the paper were checked but excluded from deposits because they cite third-party software: reference [32], https://github.com/explosion/spaCy, returned HTTP 200; its named GitHub recursive-tree API returned HTTP 200, truncated=false, listing 1,776 file blobs. This is the general spaCy library, not a c478 data deposit. Reference [40], https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1234, returned HTTP 404 (DOI Not Found); https://zenodo.org/api/records/1234 returned HTTP 500, so its files/contents could not be confirmed. The printed DOI was retained without correction. The unrelated article DOI in reference [70], https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgae052, returned HTTP 403 with a bot-check page and was not pursued.

The deposits list counts the one study-specific repository. Project/publisher landing pages, the preprint and its manuscript-source archive, an earlier presentation, and unrelated software references are documented above rather than counted as study-data deposits. The negative data finding is limited to the sources checked, particularly because publisher supplementary files could not be inspected. All network requests used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without login, access requests, or personal identifiers. Files obtained over the network were read only in memory.
